overview: This House resolution requires every member of the House, along with House officers and staff, to complete training each year of Congress on workplace rights and responsibilities, including training on preventing discrimination and harassment. These rights come from the Congressional Accountability Act of 1995, which applies workplace protection laws to Congress. Interns (including unpaid interns), fellows, and staff on loan from other federal agencies count as employees and must take the training too. The Committee on House Administration must write rules within 30 days, and people generally have 90 days to finish the training and file a certificate, with flexibility for short-term interns and people who join late in a session. The House adopted it on June 9, 2025.
for: Supporters say requiring regular training for everyone in the House, including lawmakers and interns, helps make sure people know their rights and helps prevent harassment and discrimination.
against: Critics say training alone may do little to change behavior, and the resolution leaves enforcement mostly to the committee rather than setting penalties for those who don't comply.
